topic: Talking to your therapist about pressure

slides.headline: Too hard? Too soft? Say so.
slides.sub: How to talk about pressure so your massage actually helps.

slides.title: Myth: harder is always better
slides.body: Deeper pressure isn't automatically more effective. Many people get the most out of firm but comfortable pressure that lets muscles relax, rather than bracing through every stroke.

slides.title: Use a simple 0 to 10 scale
slides.body: Tell your therapist where you are on a scale of 0 to 10. Around 5 to 7 is often comfortable and useful for most people. If you're holding your breath, it's too much.

slides.title: Speak up anytime
slides.body: You can ask for more pressure, less pressure or a different area at any point. Good therapists check in regularly, but you don't need to wait to be asked. It's your session.

slides.title: Mention what's going on
slides.body: Let them know about recent injuries, bruising easily, pregnancy, skin sensitivity or areas you'd rather avoid. It helps your therapist choose pressure and techniques that suit you.

slides.title: What's normal afterwards
slides.body: Mild tenderness for a day or two is common after firmer work. Heavy bruising or pain that keeps getting worse isn't expected, so let your therapist know so they can adjust next time.

slides.headline: Book a session that suits you
slides.body: Our remedial massage therapists tailor pressure to you and work alongside our physios when you're also doing rehab. Book online — link in bio.

caption:
Ever lain there thinking 'that's way too much' and said nothing?

Harder isn't automatically better. Many people get more out of firm but comfortable pressure that lets muscles relax. A simple 0 to 10 scale helps: around 5 to 7 is often a good zone, and if you're holding your breath, it's too much.

You can ask for more, less or a different area at any time. Mention recent injuries, easy bruising, pregnancy or areas to avoid. Mild tenderness for a day or two is common after firmer work, but pain that keeps getting worse isn't expected.
